thread.title_full: FORMER KEY WEST OFFICIAL COULD LOSE HOME'S CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY - NewsBreak

author: KATRINA NICHOLS Keys Citizen
title: FORMER KEY WEST OFFICIAL COULD LOSE HOME'S CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY - NewsBreak
text: The City of Key West is moving to revoke the Certificate of Occupancy for the Harris Avenue home of former Chief Building Official Rajindhar “Raj” Ramsingh, whose alleged misconduct in the role remains under investigation. On June 17, the city sent a certified letter to Ramsingh and his wife, Deborah Ramsingh, notifying them of significant permitting and inspection issues at their property at 2827 Harris Ave. According to the letter, acting Chief Building Official and licensed Building Code Administrator Ronald W. Wampler reviewed the property’s permit history and found multiple violations, including incomplete inspections and concealed work. To address the issues, the city outlined several corrective actions. These include revoking the current Certificate of Occupancy to prevent a sale before compliance is verified, requiring new permits from licensed contractors for all major systems, voiding all permits issued since 2021 and conducting extensive inspections and non-destructive testing of the home’s structure, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas, roofing, framing and foundation systems. If the required corrective actions are not taken, the city may order the property to be vacated and electrical service disconnected. A new Certificate of Occupancy will only be issued once all deficiencies are corrected and verified by professional engineers, architects and licensed contractors, according to the letter. These steps come amid Ramsingh’s mounting legal troubles. On May 7, the Monroe County State Attorney’s Office announced a third indictment against Ramsingh, charging him with organized fraud for allegedly running a scheme between January 2022 and February 2024 to unlawfully obtain more than $50,000 through fraudulent representations. The charge, a first-degree felony, carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison. Ramsingh was released on a $50,000 bond. Prosecutors allege Ramsingh falsified building permit records for various Key West properties between 2021 and 2024 for personal gain and to benefit his private construction company, StrykkerAvery Homes LLC. In April, Ramsingh and his brother, former Key West City Attorney Ron Ramsingh, and retired Code Compliance Director James Young were indicted for evidence tampering and obstruction of justice following a joint investigation by the Monroe County State Attorney’s Office and the FBI. Since the indictments, Ramsingh has been placed on indefinite unpaid administrative leave. In response to the allegations, the Key West City Commission on June 4 approved a full review of all building permits issued between 2020 and 2025. This is a developing story. Updates will be provided as information becomes available. Subscribe to The Key West Citizen
